title: Biblical Syncretism Dossiers — Son Prefiguration / Narrow Way / Lion-Whelp Wave 24
purpose: Promote the strongest newly recovered Son-side prefiguration relations into the live Bible comparison field: the reported pre-meme-cross narrow-way painting, the 2017–2019 Passion prehistory, and the Dan/Judah Lion-Whelp hinge. Keep primary-artifact recovery, chronology and mismatches visible.

new_relations.title: Before the meme-cross: a reported narrow path through death-shadow toward light
new_relations.project_anchor: Project testimony describes a painting made around 2018–2019, reportedly later circulated on the Farm, showing a narrow/straight path through a night/death landscape toward distant light, with a gate, black water, skeletons/death remains, cliffs and precarious footing. The primary image/post has not yet been recovered into the repository.
new_relations.what_happened: The visual sequence reportedly existed before or around the approach to the later meme-cross period. Its value is developmental: threshold, narrow passage, death landscape and light appear spatially before mature Son-as-Door / death-return architecture.
new_relations.wording_status: later project recollection of a visual artifact; image and timestamp recovery pending

scene_context.summary: Reported artwork topology: shore/death-field -> gate/hostile oversight -> narrow precarious path through darkness -> distant light.

relation_argument.why_dense: The overlap is not a single word. Gate, path, death-shadow and light form one directional route in the reported image, matching several biblical passage-functions that mature Potatoverse theology later develops separately.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: If the original image/post is recovered with a pre-meme-cross date, it would become one of the stronger pieces of prior symbolic topology in the Son chronology.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The project can presently record a strong remembered structural comparison. Until the image and date are recovered, it cannot claim independently verified prefiguration or prophecy.

scripture_context.literary_context: Matthew 7 contrasts narrow gate/way with broad destruction; Psalm 23 describes walking through death-shadow; John 8 presents following Jesus as walking in light rather than darkness.
scripture_context.canonical_context: These are different passages and genres. Wave 24 compares their functions to one visual route without claiming the artist consciously fused them.

discovery_history.source_direction: Reported artwork first; verse-level comparison later. Primary artifact recovery remains decisive.

new_relations.mismatch: No recovered image or contemporaneous explanation currently proves that these verses were intended sources. Tunnel/light, night, bones and dangerous paths are broader religious/artistic motifs as well.

new_relations.title: Death becomes landscape: bones, dark water and precarious passage
new_relations.project_anchor: The same reported painting places skeletons/death remains beside the route and black water below/alongside a precarious passage.
new_relations.wording_status: later visual recollection; primary artifact pending

scene_context.summary: The walker is reportedly surrounded by visible signs of death rather than meeting death as one isolated event.

relation_argument.why_dense: Ezekiel makes bones a whole valley and Psalm/Jonah make deep waters a death-near boundary. Those functions illuminate why the painting’s remembered bones and black water matter as environmental hazards rather than decorative horror.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: These are secondary visual neighbors only; no direct biblical source should be asserted without recovering the artwork/context.

new_relations.mismatch: Ezekiel’s bones are restored to life and Jonah is delivered from a specific descent narrative; those reversals are not visibly established in the reported painting.

new_relations.title: Dan and Judah both receive the Lion’s-Whelp image
new_relations.project_anchor: The Son corpus later develops Lion of the World / lion’s-whelp language and tribe-of-Dan identification. Earlier persona material also preserves a Kitty/KittyStyle lead, while Leo functions as a low-weight extra-biblical personal symbol.
new_relations.what_happened: A close biblical comparison shows that lion-whelp language is not exclusive to Judah: Genesis 49:9 applies it to Judah, while Deuteronomy 33:22 applies it to Dan.
new_relations.wording_status: later explicit project Lion/Dan synthesis; Kitty primary-source recovery still desirable

scene_context.summary: The relation is lexical and genealogical-symbolic rather than one dated physical event.

correspondences: same lion-cub image applied to two distinct tribes
project already combines Lion with Dan while also engaging Christological Judah material
relation_argument.why_dense: The Bible itself supplies the bridge the project was previously constructing by association: Dan and Judah are both explicitly given lion-cub/whelp imagery in separate tribal blessings.
relation_argument.why_it_matters: It permits a more precise comparison: the project can hold Dan and Judah as distinct roles connected by a shared symbol rather than collapsing one tribe into the other.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: This establishes a genuine biblical lexical overlap between Dan and Judah. It does not establish modern tribal descent, messiahship or supernatural identity.

scripture_context.literary_context: Genesis 49 and Deuteronomy 33 are distinct tribal blessing traditions. Judah’s passage develops rule/scepter imagery; Dan’s Deuteronomy blessing uses lion-cub imagery without making Dan Judah.
scripture_context.canonical_context: Shared imagery does not erase tribal distinction.

discovery_history.project_anchor_date: Lion/Dan material developed before formal comparison
discovery_history.scripture_explicit_at_time: lion-whelp wording later became explicit in project discussion
discovery_history.source_direction: Project Lion/Dan field first; precise Dan/Judah lexical hinge formalized later.

new_relations.mismatch: The project must not infer genealogy from symbolic similarity, and it should preserve the distinct contexts of the two blessings.

new_relations.title: Lion announced, Lamb seen: the Son’s Lion/Lamb double-image
new_relations.project_anchor: The Son chronology carries Lamb recognition language from the prison period and later Lion/Lion-of-the-World language. The two images were often treated as separate title families.
new_relations.what_happened: Revelation 5 itself puts the two together: the expected conquering Lion of Judah/Root of David is announced, but the visionary sees a Lamb standing as slain.
new_relations.wording_status: project titles/recollections precede detailed Revelation synthesis

scene_context.summary: This relation spans the Son identity genealogy rather than one event: remembered Lamb recognition -> later Lion language -> later formal Lion/Lamb synthesis.

project_sequence: reported external Jesus/Lamb recognition in prison
biblical_sequence: Lion of Judah/Root of David announced as conqueror
Lamb is seen standing as slain
correspondences: Lion and Lamb applied to one christological figure
victory does not erase wounding/death imagery
relation_argument.why_dense: The text itself resolves what could look like contradictory project symbols: Lion and Lamb need not be alternative identities; Revelation deliberately joins strength/kingship and sacrificial wounding.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: This is a strong canonical comparator for the project’s Lion/Lamb double-image. It does not independently validate the modern Son as Revelation’s Christ.

new_relations.mismatch: Revelation’s titles and visionary role belong to its own Christology and apocalypse; later project reuse is appropriation/comparison.

new_relations.title: Dan is not only Lion: Judge, serpent and roadside danger complicate the symbol
new_relations.project_anchor: The project sometimes treats Dan as a positive Son/Lion identity. Genesis 49 gives a less flattering and more complex Dan cluster that should remain visible.

relation_argument.why_dense: The same Dan blessing family that supplies judgment also gives serpent/road imagery and an appeal for salvation. This prevents selective use of only the lion-whelp verse from another blessing tradition.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: Dan should be treated as a mixed biblical symbolic field, not a simple badge of positive Lion identity.

new_relations.mismatch: Genesis 49 is poetic tribal blessing material, not a direct modern personality map.

new_relations.title: A provisional pre-meme-cross table-flip may reproduce Temple-confrontation-before-Passion order
new_relations.project_anchor: Later Tim recollection places a table-flipping confrontation before the meme-cross, in response to people allegedly selling the Son’s story short, changing his image and turning resistance into further spectacle. Exact primary dating remains unrecovered.
new_relations.what_happened: The comparison becomes interesting only as chronology: Synoptic Gospels place the Temple table-overturning conflict immediately in the final Jerusalem corridor that intensifies the move toward Jesus’ death.
new_relations.wording_status: later recollection; original post/recording and exact date not recovered

scene_context.summary: Reported resistance to perceived commodification/story-control before later symbolic crucifixion/death sequence.

correspondences: table overturning tied to perceived corrupt exchange
relation_argument.why_dense: The value is chronological, not lexical. If an original 2018 source verifies table-flipping before the meme-cross, the order itself becomes a meaningful Passion comparator.
relation_argument.maximum_claim: The sequence is currently provisional because the table-flip date is not source-secure. It should be promoted further only after primary recovery.

new_relations.mismatch: The Gospel scene is the Jerusalem Temple and its commerce; the project recollection concerns modern story/image exploitation. John also places the cleansing early rather than immediately before the Passion, so canonical chronology is not uniform.

higher_order_results: The strongest new visual relation is route topology, not a single symbol: gate -> narrow way -> death-shadow -> light.
The strongest new Lion relation is lexical and canonical: Dan and Judah both receive lion-whelp/cub imagery; Revelation then joins Judah-Lion and slain-standing Lamb.
Kitty can become useful chronology evidence only if its pre-Lion use is recovered from primary archives. Leo remains low-weight cultural resonance.

The reported painting and table-flip are potentially valuable because they may predate the mature crucifixion theology; therefore primary recovery and dating matter more than adding further speculative verse matches.
Wave 24 strengthens the archive by distinguishing prior symbol, later interpretation and exact biblical comparator rather than treating every later resonance as prophecy.
